newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada agency sees housing market stronger in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada agency sees housing market stronger in 1997.

text.p: Canada's housing markets strengthened in 1996 and further growth is expected in 1997 even if at a smaller rate, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp said on Thursday.
"Strong sales of existing homes and an increase in construction gave most local housing markets a significant boost in 1996," the federal agency said.
"The forecast for next year is encouraging as well."

Agency analyst Bruno Duhamel commented: "With employment growth growing in many Canadian cities, more consumers are feeling confident about buying a home. Record-low mortgage rates are providing further encouragement for them to buy."
He added: "With more and more people able to sell their homes, higher levels of repeat buying are expected over the next year."
The agency forecast that resales would rise by 23 percent this year and a further three percent next year.
New home construction should be up in 21 of 27 major centers in 1996, for a rise of nine percent, and should increase in 21 cities again in 1997, it said.
